page: Hetzner Cloud cpx52 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC processor running under the QEMU hypervisor. It features 12 shared vCPUs with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, 23.0 GB of system memory (approximately 1.95 GB per core), and 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3041.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2075.0, both placing in the top 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 220.5 GB/sec for read-only operations and 143.81 GB/sec for write operations. However, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 36626.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12171.0, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPU allocation. Small-model LLM inference is highly efficient, generating 304.2 tokens per second on a 135M model.

The cpx52 instance offers high resource density and cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from strong single-core execution and fast NVMe storage, but do not require dedicated CPU cores. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core loads. This server is well-suited for web serving, application hosting, lightweight database operations, software compilation, and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks.
